rules.title: Security deposit capped at one month's rent
rules.requirement: A landlord may not demand or receive a security deposit (however labeled) of more than one month's rent, in addition to first month's rent. Small landlords (natural persons or all-natural-person LLCs owning no more than two rental properties with no more than four units in total) may charge up to two months' rent, but not to service members.
rules.key_value: 1 month's rent (2 months for qualifying small landlords)
rules.coverage_conditions: Security for rental agreements for residential property used as the tenant's dwelling; applies to security collected or demanded on or after July 1, 2024.
rules.exemptions: Small landlord exception: a natural person (including family trust settlors/beneficiaries) or an LLC whose members are all natural persons, owning no more than two residential rental properties with no more than four dwelling units offered for rent in total, may take up to two months' rent; this does not apply if the prospective tenant is a service member. Advance payment of at least six months' rent is allowed on leases of six months or longer. Security collected before July 1, 2024 is not covered.
rules.quoted_span: a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy.
rules.penalty: Bad-faith demand or retention may result in statutory damages of up to twice the amount of the security plus actual damages (§ 1950.5(m)).

exemption_tests.description: Small landlord (natural person/family trust or LLC with all natural-person members) owning no more than two residential rental properties with no more than four units in total may charge up to two months' rent; not applicable to service-member tenants.

rules.title: Higher security charged to service members must be explained and refunded after six months
rules.requirement: If a landlord charges a service member a higher-than-standard deposit because of credit or housing history, the landlord must explain it in writing by lease signing. The extra amount must be returned after no more than six months if the tenant is not behind on rent.
rules.coverage_conditions: Service members (as defined in Mil. & Vet. Code § 400) renting residential property they will live in.
rules.quoted_span: On or after April 1, 2025, if a landlord or its agent charges a service member who rents residential property in which the service member will reside a higher than standard or advertised security

rules.title: Deposit return within 21 days with itemized statement
rules.requirement: Within 21 calendar days after you move out, the landlord must return your remaining deposit along with an itemized statement of deductions and copies of receipts or invoices (or a good-faith estimate). Receipts are not required if deductions total $125 or less, unless you ask for them within 14 days. Bad-faith retention can cost the landlord up to twice the deposit.
rules.key_value: 21 calendar days; up to 2x deposit statutory damages for bad faith
rules.exemptions: Documentation (receipts) not required if repair/cleaning deductions do not exceed $125 or the tenant validly waived, unless the tenant requests documentation within 14 days.
rules.quoted_span: No later than 21 calendar days after the tenant has vacated the premises, but not earlier than the time that either the landlord or the tenant provides a notice to terminate the tenancy under Section 1946 or 1946.1
rules.penalty: Landlord forfeits any claim to the security for bad-faith noncompliance with subdivision (h); bad-faith retention may subject landlord to statutory damages of up to twice the security plus actual damages.

rules.title: Electronic return of deposit when tenant paid electronically
rules.requirement: If you paid your deposit or rent electronically, the landlord must return the remaining deposit electronically to an account you designate in writing, unless you agree in writing to another method. The landlord must tell you about this right before the tenancy ends.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenants who paid security or rent to the landlord electronically.
rules.exemptions: Not applicable if landlord and tenant agreed in writing to another return method; notice requirement does not apply to terminations under CCP § 1161(2)-(4).
rules.citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5(h)(1)(A)(ii) (as amended by AB 414, Stats. 2025, Ch. 340)
rules.quoted_span: If the landlord received the security or rental payments from the tenant electronically, the landlord shall return the remainder of the security electronically

rules.title: Move-in and move-out photographs required for deposit deductions
rules.requirement: For tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025, landlords must photograph the unit at move-in. Since April 1, 2025, landlords must also photograph the unit after move-out (before and after repairs or cleaning) and include the photos with any deductions.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental units; move-in photos for tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025.
rules.quoted_span: Beginning April 1, 2025, the landlord shall take photographs of the unit within a reasonable time after the possession of the unit is returned to the landlord

rules.title: Limits on deposit deductions (no ordinary wear and tear or preexisting damage)
rules.requirement: Landlords may deduct only reasonable amounts for unpaid rent, damage beyond ordinary wear and tear, cleaning to move-in condition, and authorized property restoration. They may not charge for preexisting damage, ordinary wear and tear, or unnecessary professional cleaning.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord shall not assert a claim against the tenant or the security for damages to the premises or any defective conditions that preexisted the tenancy, for ordinary wear and tear or the effects thereof

rules.title: Tenant right to pre-move-out initial inspection
rules.requirement: Before the tenancy ends, the landlord must tell you in writing that you can request an initial inspection, which may be held up to two weeks before move-out. The landlord must give you an itemized list of proposed deductions so you can fix the problems first.
rules.key_value: Inspection no earlier than 2 weeks before move-out; 48 hours' notice
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies, except those terminated under CCP § 1161(2), (3), or (4).
rules.exemptions: Does not apply when the tenancy is terminated under CCP § 1161(2), (3), or (4).
rules.quoted_span: the landlord shall notify the tenant in writing of the tenant’s option to request an initial inspection and of the tenant’s right to be present at the inspection.

rules.title: No nonrefundable security deposits
rules.requirement: A lease may not call any deposit or security "nonrefundable."
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential leases and rental agreements.
rules.quoted_span: A lease or rental agreement shall not contain a provision characterizing any security as “nonrefundable.”

notes: The source is the official text of Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5, last amended by AB 414 (Stats. 2025, Ch. 340), effective January 1, 2026. The document doesn't say which provisions AB 414 changed. I dated the electronic-return rule 2026-01-01 based on outside knowledge of AB 414, so that date carries lower confidence. The deposit cap's July 1, 2024 date comes from subdivision (c)(6). Whether the small-landlord exception (two months' rent) applies depends on who owns the property and their total holdings, which an assessor record can't show. Section 1950.6 (application screening fees) is mentioned only as a cross-reference and was not extracted. I left out the provisions on transferring the deposit to a new owner (subdivisions (i)–(l)), since they cover what happens when a property is sold, not a tenant's direct deposit rights. I also left out the small-claims and proof-of-deposit procedure rules ((o), (p)).
